scope: Curated local-history and place reporting; no original 2026 probability model.
description: Additional independently sourced local context for selected congressional district guides. All other district guides render official Census geography, the election atlas and ACS data without invented places.

IA-01.title: The Mississippi River, a university town, and one of America's tightest House rematches.
IA-01.geography_deck: Twenty southeast Iowa counties connect the Iowa City area, the Iowa side of the Quad Cities, Mississippi River communities and farming towns stretching toward central Iowa.

major_communities.name: Iowa City
major_communities.note: University of Iowa and a major regional health and education center.

major_communities.name: Coralville and North Liberty
major_communities.note: Growing communities in the Iowa City metropolitan area.

major_communities.name: Davenport and Bettendorf
major_communities.note: The Iowa side of the Quad Cities, a Mississippi River metro with manufacturing and transport connections.

major_communities.name: Clinton
major_communities.note: A Mississippi River city in the district's northeast.

major_communities.name: Muscatine
major_communities.note: A Mississippi River industrial and agricultural community.

major_communities.name: Burlington
major_communities.note: A southeast Iowa river port; Des Moines County is not the city of Des Moines.

major_communities.name: Fort Madison and Keokuk
major_communities.note: Historic river communities near the Missouri and Illinois borders.

major_communities.name: Pella and Newton
major_communities.note: Interior Iowa communities linking the district to central Iowa.

character.title: Two different urban anchors
character.text: Iowa City's university-centered economy and Davenport's Quad Cities manufacturing-and-river economy give the district different local interests.

character.title: A river-and-rural coalition
character.text: Mississippi River towns coexist with agricultural counties, small manufacturers and central Iowa communities.

character.title: Do not confuse the 2020 boundaries
character.text: The district's current 20-county configuration began with the 2022 election. The candidate's six-vote 2020 win occurred in the old 2nd District, not today's IA-01.
